newsitem.title: FRANCE: Council of Europe ends HR monitoring in Romania.
newsitem.headline: Council of Europe ends HR monitoring in Romania.

text.p: The Council of Europe decided on Thursday to end human rights monitoring in Romania but said Bucharest should enact further reforms or face a return of monitoring.
"We were strongly impressed...by the change in the political climate and the open-mindedness of the new team in power," said Gunnar Jannson, the Council deputy who sponsored the move.
The 40-state Council, which monitors democracy and human rights in Europe, reserved the right to reinstate human rights monitoring if sufficient progress were not made within a year.
The decision comes ahead of a NATO summit in Madrid in July and could be a boost to Bucharest's hopes of being considered as a candidate to join an expanded NATO.

The Council said the reformist Romanian government which took over from ex-communists last year must improve its performance on judicial independence, homosexual rights, freedom of expression and prison conditions.
It also said it must ensure the restitution of goods confiscated under the former communist regime or guarantee compensation.
Romania has ratified the European treaty on human rights and conventions against torture and protecting national minorities.
